data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The hypothesis that S(13) = 45 is optimal is best supported by a structural absence of 44-comparator networks, which can be demonstrated by observing that local search algorithms (e.g., simulated annealing) exhibit a sharp phase transition: they readily find valid 45-comparator networks but systematically fail to find any valid 44-comparator networks under a fixed computational budget.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The simulated annealing search finds a valid 44-comparator network within the fixed budget, falsifying the structural absence hypothesis and proving S(13) <= 44.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A formal proof is discovered showing S(13) <= 44, rendering the simulation-based discrimination obsolete.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Implement a simulated annealing search over comparator sequences of length L.
